messages.text: My nerd qx stopped mining and i noticed the display went blank but fan are still running
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Hi Bobby, I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this one to me.

Blank screen with fans still spinning is usually one of two things: the display/firmware has hung, or the chips have dropped out. Let's find out which.

First check: on the same network, can you still reach the miner's web UI? Open its IP in a browser (check your router's client list for something like "nerdqaxe" or "bitaxe" if you don't have the IP saved).

Tell me which of these you get:
1. The web UI loads and shows a hashrate
2. The web UI loads but hashrate is 0 or "0 chips" / ASIC error
3. Nothing loads at all

Thanks. No web UI plus a blank screen points at the unit not fully booting, even though the fans spin (fans run on raw 5V, so they spin even when the board is hung).

Next check, a clean power cycle:
1. Unplug the power cable from the miner (not just the wall switch)
2. Wait 30 seconds
3. Plug it back in and watch the screen for the first 30 seconds

Tell me what happens: does the screen show anything at all (logo, text, backlight glow), or does it stay completely dark while the fans ramp up?
no logo, or backlight but ramp and stay at that speed

That pattern matters: fans ramping to one fixed speed and staying there means the firmware never took control of them. The board is powering up electrically but not booting.

Before we call it a board fault, we rule out the power supply, which is the most common cause of exactly this on the Nerd boards (the stock bricks sag under load).

Do you have another supply you can try? For the NerdQX you want a good 5V supply rated at least 5A (or a quality USB-C PD charger plus the right cable, if that's how yours connects). Also swap the cable itself, a marginal cable does the same thing.

Two questions so I know what we're working with:
1. How does your unit connect to power, barrel jack or USB-C?
2. Do you have another supply/cable in the house to test with?
the new yellow connection

I want to be sure I'm picturing the right connector before I send you down the wrong path. Can you snap a quick photo of where the power cable plugs into the miner (and of the supply's label, the small print with the volts and amps)?

If it's the yellow XT60-style plug, that's the higher current input and it only runs properly off the matching brick, so the supply's rating on the label is exactly what I need to see.
xt60 connector

Good, that's the 12V XT60 input.

One decisive test before we talk hardware, and it doesn't need a second brick. The NerdQX controller (the ESP32) can be powered over its USB-C port alone:

1. Unplug the XT60 power
2. Connect the miner's USB-C port to a computer with a data cable (not a charge-only cable)
3. Watch the screen

Tell me what happens:
1. The screen lights up / shows text on USB power alone
2. The computer detects a new USB serial device but the screen stays dark
3. Nothing at all, no screen, no device detected

If you're on Windows, "new device" chime or Device Manager under Ports (COM & LPT) is what to look for; on a Mac it shows as a usbserial or usbmodem device.
no does not light up, but a blue is on the back of the display, and the compuiter keeps climing no connection

The blue LED tells me the 5V rail is alive, so power is getting in. But the computer seeing nothing means the ESP32 controller isn't enumerating, and that's either the cable or the board.

Cables are the usual culprit here, most USB-C cables lying around are charge-only. Try one you know moves files (one you've used to transfer photos off a phone), and use a port directly on the computer, not a hub.

Tell me after that: does the computer still say no connection?
in and out

That's actually useful: connecting and dropping over and over means the ESP32 is alive but resetting in a loop, not dead.

We can stop the loop by forcing it into download mode, which also sets up a clean reflash (a full reflash from 0x0000 is the standard fix for a NerdQX that boot loops):

1. Unplug everything (XT60 and USB)
2. Find the small BOOT button on the board, next to the USB-C port
3. Hold BOOT down, plug the USB-C cable in while still holding, keep holding about 3 seconds, then release

Tell me: with BOOT held, does the computer show a stable device that stays connected instead of coming and going?
yes
Good, that confirms the controller is healthy. Now we reflash it properly. Give me a moment, I'm pulling the current firmware version off Harlo's site so I point you at the right file.
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · NerdQaxe++ full flash esptool offset 0x0000 web flasher

Right, here's the fix. We do a factory install from the ROM bootloader, which is the standard cure for a NerdQX that boot loops with a dark screen.

Use Chrome or Edge (Firefox and Safari can't talk to the device):

1. Go to https://harlolabs.com/ and click "Download Latest Firmware"
2. Pick your exact miner model in the dropdown (this matters, a wrong image makes it worse, so if you're unsure of the exact variant tell me what's printed on the board or send a photo of it and I'll confirm)
3. Keep the XT60 power unplugged, hold BOOT and plug the USB-C in, release after 3 seconds, like you just did
4. Click C. miner, tick the acknowledgement, then Erase & install
5. Leave USB connected until it finishes, close any other serial tool first


Erasing wipes the partition table, both OTA slots and stored settings, so it clears a half-written update and guarantees it boots from a known-good image.
 You will have to re-enter Wi-Fi and your pool settings afterwards, so have those handy.

Run it and tell me what the installation log says at the end, and whether the screen comes up when you reconnect the XT60.
i have the nerd qx which firmware do i use

Don't guess on this one, the image has to match the ASIC on your board. The telltale is the chip marking:

- BM1366 = NerdQAxe
- BM1368 = NerdQAxe+
- BM1370 = NerdQAxe++ (or ++ Hydro, marked "Hydro")

Quickest way: take a photo of the board with the heatsinks in view and the small print on the chips/silkscreen (a phone macro shot works), and post it here. I'll tell you exactly which entry to pick in the dropdown.

If you still have the box or the product page from your order, the model name on there works too.
worked great thank u

Great news, Bobby. The reflash cleared it, so it was a corrupted firmware image, not a hardware fault.

Two things worth doing now it's up:
1. Check your pool dashboard in 15 to 30 minutes and confirm the worker is showing shares, since the erase wiped the old pool and Wi-Fi settings
2. If you do an OTA update later, don't cut power while it's writing, that's what usually causes this

Anything else on it, I'm here, and the Discord is fast too: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf (JD is @nullhashrate there). Happy mining.
